descriptionChirho: A young bovine animal, used literally in the NT both for the fatted calf killed in celebration (Luke 15:23) and for sacrificial calves (Heb 9:12,19). The two clusters differ only in grammatical number: singular (N-AMS, N-DMS) vs plural (N-GMP). Multilingual evidence confirms uniform semantics: Spanish 'becerro/becerros', Hindi बछड़ा/बछड़ों, Arabic العجل/عجول, Korean 송아지/송아지들, Swahili ndama throughout. No semantic distinction warrants separate senses; this is purely inflectional variation of one concrete noun denoting a young cow or bull.
